candidate_matches.similarity_basis: Direct named existing contract and code trace, not embedding estimate.
candidate_matches.title: TRACE and CONNECT enable policy
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall disable `TRACE` and `CONNECT` routing by default, so that both yield the unsupported-method result whatever the path, and shall provide a router policy that enables each of them separately, after which an enabled method routes like any other method and is registered only by naming it.
candidate_matches.reason: Legacy default-off TRACE/CONNECT routing conflicts with explicit common Express method registration; preserve legacy switches only in identified extension/WS profile.

acceptance_criteria.text: Under the default policy, `TRACE /x` and `CONNECT /x` yield unsupported method whether or not any route matches `/x`. [D-067]

With only `TRACE` enabled, a registered `TRACE /x` route is matched, `TRACE /y` with no matching pattern yields no match, `TRACE` on a path with only a `GET` route yields method mismatch, and `CONNECT /x` still yields unsupported method. [wave decision: TRACE/CONNECT policy]

With `CONNECT` enabled, `CONNECT` behaves as `TRACE` does in the previous criterion, and in neither case does a registration under `Method.any()` serve the enabled method. [wave decision: TRACE/CONNECT policy; D-036]

candidate_matches.title: Route pattern syntax and registration-time validation
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall accept route patterns made of literal segments and `:name` variable segments, where a variable matches exactly one non-empty path segment and never crosses `/`, and shall fail registration with a configuration error for a pattern that contains Express wildcard or regular-expression syntax, an empty variable name, a variable name repeated within the pattern, or an empty segment.
candidate_matches.reason: Legacy string syntax rejects wildcard/optional/quoted/escape/partial parameters that common Express5 accepts.

acceptance_criteria.text: `/users/:id` matches `/users/42` with `id` = `42`, and matches neither `/users`, `/users/` nor `/users/42/posts`. [D-047]
Registering a pattern containing `?`, `*`, `+`, `(` or `)` fails with a configuration error. [D-048]

Registering `/a/:` or `/a/:id/:id` fails with a configuration error at registration time. [wave decision: pattern validation] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-2 SDS-AC-5] The error is a `RoutingConfigException` thrown from `add` before freeze, naming the pattern.
Registering `/a//b` fails with a configuration error, while `/` and a pattern with one trailing slash such as `/users/` are accepted. [loop W residual: empty segment]

candidate_matches.title: Engine-free request path validator
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall provide an engine-free path validator, run before the router lookup by the wave 3 dispatcher and every adapter, that inspects the raw request path without decoding it and rejects malformed percent-encoding, percent-encoded bytes that are not valid UTF-8, raw non-ASCII characters, an encoded `/`, an encoded or raw `NUL`, and any `.` or `..` segment in raw or percent-encoded form, matching the rules TinyHttpd's parser applies.
candidate_matches.reason: Pre-routing decoded slash/NUL/dot rejection conflicts with common raw-path matching/capture decode semantics.

acceptance_criteria.text: The validator rejects `/a%2`, `/a%zz`, `/a%C3` (truncated UTF-8), `/a%FF`, a path containing a raw character above U+007F, `/a%2Fb`, `/a%2fb`, `/a%00`, a path containing a raw U+0000, `/./a`, `/a/..`, `/a/%2e`, `/a/%2E%2e` and `/a/.%2e/b`. [D-052] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-2 SDS-AC-6] A segment equal to '.' or '..' after decoding, a malformed %XX, an encoded '/', NUL or an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence yields false.
The validator also rejects, as TinyHttpd's request-target parser does, a path containing a raw space, a raw control character U+0001..U+001F, U+007F or `#`. [D-052]
The validator accepts `/users/42`, `/files/%252e`, `/caf%C3%A9` and `/a/.hidden`, and its result is the same whether or not a query string follows the path. [D-052; D-051]

The validator returns an accept or reject decision without returning a decoded path, and the router lookup API has no result variant for a rejected path. [loop W residual; wave decision: path validation before lookup]

candidate_matches.title: Strict default matching with single percent-decoding
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall match a request path against patterns ignoring the query string, decoding each path segment exactly once, and by default comparing case-sensitively with a significant trailing slash and with an empty segment never matching a literal or variable segment, returning path parameter values as decoded once and otherwise as received.
candidate_matches.reason: Strict decoded segment matching conflicts with raw-path compiled matcher and new defaults.

acceptance_criteria.text: `/users?id=1` and `/users` both match `/users`. [D-049]
Under the default policy `/Users` and `/users/` do not match `/users`, and `/users/` matches only a pattern registered as `/users/`. [D-050]

`/files/%252e` matched against `/files/:name` yields `name` = `%2e`, and `/caf%C3%A9` matches the literal pattern `/café`. [D-051] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-2 SDS-AC-8] Each segment is decoded %XX exactly once as UTF-8 and '+' stays '+'.
Under the default policy `/a//b` matches neither `/a/:x/b` nor `/a/b` and reaches the no-match result when no other pattern matches. [wave decision: path-form policy]

candidate_matches.title: Path-form router policies
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall provide three independent router policy switches, each off by default, that merge repeated slashes, ignore one trailing slash, and compare literal segments case-insensitively, with path parameter values returned as received under every switch and the configuration API names on `RestApp` left to wave 3.
candidate_matches.reason: All-off defaults conflict with Express5 case/trailing defaults; retain explicit strict and WS profile.

acceptance_criteria.text: With repeated-slash merging on, `/a//b` matches `/a/b`; with it off, it does not. [D-053]

With trailing-slash ignoring on, `/users/` matches `/users` and `/users` matches a pattern registered as `/users/`; `/users//` does not match `/users` unless repeated-slash merging is also on; the root path `/` is never stripped to an empty path. [D-053]

With case-insensitive matching on, `/USERS/Bob` matches `/users/:name` and yields `name` = `Bob`, and the comparison is locale-independent (the same result under a Turkish default locale for `/LIST` against `/list`). [D-053; wave decision: path-form policy] Matching and prefix-middleware selection use the same locale-independent Unicode code-point folding policy on Java8 and Java17, including supplementary characters.

Each switch can be set without the others, the switches are fixed when the router is built, and a router built without setting any of them behaves as the strict default. [wave decision: path-form policy] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-2 SDS-AC-10] The router copies the immutable `RouterPolicy` at construction and offers no setter afterwards.

candidate_matches.title: Per-method pattern priority
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall, for the request method, pick the most specific matching pattern among the routes of that method, comparing patterns segment by segment from the left so that the first differing segment decides and a literal segment beats a variable segment regardless of registration order.
candidate_matches.reason: Specificity precedence conflicts with registration order.

acceptance_criteria.text: With `GET /users/:id` registered before `GET /users/me`, a `GET /users/me` lookup returns the `/users/me` handler and `GET /users/42` returns the `/users/:id` handler; the result is the same with the opposite registration order. [D-054]
With `GET /a/:x/c` and `GET /a/b/:y`, a `GET /a/b/c` lookup returns the `/a/b/:y` handler. [D-055]
With `GET /users/me` and `DELETE /users/:id`, a `DELETE /users/me` lookup returns the matched result for `DELETE /users/:id`. [wave decision: per-method priority]

candidate_matches.similarity_basis: Direct named existing contract and code trace, not embedding estimate.
candidate_matches.title: Conflict detection at route-table freeze
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall provide a route-table freeze, which wave 4 calls inside `listen()` before any socket is bound, that raises a configuration error naming both conflicting registrations when two registrations of the same route kind share a method and have the same pattern or patterns that differ only in variable names, comparing patterns normalised under the active path-form policies, and when a `TRACE` or `CONNECT` route is registered while that method's routing is disabled.
candidate_matches.reason: Freeze duplicate conflict rejection conflicts with duplicate Route layers and live registration.

acceptance_criteria.text: Registering `GET /a` twice, or `GET /a` and a `MethodSet` registration containing `GET` on `/a`, makes the freeze raise a configuration error. [D-056]
Registering `GET /a/:x` and `GET /a/:y` makes the freeze raise a configuration error, while `GET /a/:x` and `POST /a/:y` freeze without error. [D-057]

The configuration error message names the method and the pattern of both conflicting registrations, and registration itself does not raise it before the freeze. [D-058] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-2 SDS-AC-12] The freeze throws one `RoutingConfigException` whose message has one line per conflicting pair, "METHOD pattern conflicts with METHOD pattern".

With case-insensitive matching on, `GET /Users` and `GET /users` conflict at freeze; with trailing-slash ignoring on, `GET /a` and `GET /a/` conflict; under the strict default neither pair conflicts. [loop W residual: normalised conflicts] Case-insensitive conflict keys use the same Unicode code-point folding as runtime literal/prefix matching, including supplementary characters.

Registering a `TRACE` route while `TRACE` routing is disabled makes the freeze raise a configuration error, and likewise for `CONNECT`; a WebSocket registration and a `GET` registration on the same pattern freeze without error. [loop W residual; D-068] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-2 SDS-AC-14] The freeze error line reads "METHOD pattern registered while METHOD routing is disabled".

candidate_matches.title: Method-mismatch result and Allow set
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall return the method-mismatch result when the path matches but no route of the request method matches it and no earlier result applies, carrying an `Allow` set that is the union of the methods of every route whose pattern matches the path, plus `HEAD` wherever `GET` is present and `OPTIONS` always, with a WebSocket route counted as `GET`.
candidate_matches.reason: 405/Allow outcome changes to common404 and separate ordered OPTIONS accumulation.

acceptance_criteria.text: With `Method.any().except(Method.DELETE)` registered on `/r`, `DELETE /r` yields method mismatch with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `OPTIONS`. [D-061; T02] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-6] The `Allow` set iterates and prints in `Method` declaration order.
With `POST /a/:id` and `GET /a/me`, `PUT /a/me` yields method mismatch with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `OPTIONS`. [wave decision: Allow sets]
With only `POST /p`, `GET /p` yields method mismatch with `Allow` = `POST`, `OPTIONS` (no `HEAD`). [wave decision: Allow sets]
With a WebSocket route and a `POST` route on `/w`, `PUT /w` yields method mismatch with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `OPTIONS`. [wave decision: Allow sets]

candidate_matches.title: Automatic HEAD resolution
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall resolve a `HEAD` request for which no `HEAD` route matches the path to the most specific matching HTTP `GET` route (never a WebSocket route), returned as matched with the automatic-`HEAD` flag set, and shall give a matching explicit `HEAD` route precedence over this resolution.
candidate_matches.reason: Global explicit HEAD precedence changes to per-Route fallback in ordered stack.

acceptance_criteria.text: With only `GET /x`, `HEAD /x` yields matched with the `GET` handler, actual method `GET` and the automatic-`HEAD` flag set. [D-062]
With `GET /x` and `HEAD /x`, `HEAD /x` yields matched with the `HEAD` handler and the flag clear. [D-063]
With `HEAD /x/:id` and `GET /x/me`, `HEAD /x/me` yields the `HEAD /x/:id` route with the flag clear. [wave decision: per-method priority]

candidate_matches.title: Automatic OPTIONS result
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall return the automatic-OPTIONS result, carrying the same `Allow` set as the method-mismatch result, for an `OPTIONS` request to a matched path when no `OPTIONS` route matches it, and shall give a matching explicit `OPTIONS` route precedence.
candidate_matches.reason: Automatic OPTIONS204 changes to terminal200 with exact Allow and body.

acceptance_criteria.text: With `GET /x` and `POST /x`, `OPTIONS /x` yields automatic OPTIONS with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `OPTIONS`. [D-064]
With `GET /x` and `OPTIONS /x`, `OPTIONS /x` yields matched with the `OPTIONS` handler. [D-065]
With only a WebSocket route on `/w`, `OPTIONS /w` yields automatic OPTIONS with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`. [wave decision: Allow sets]

candidate_matches.title: Unsupported-method result for unknown tokens
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall match the raw method token against `Method` constant names exactly and case-sensitively and return the unsupported-method result, whatever the path, for every token that is not a `Method` constant name.
candidate_matches.reason: Nine-case unsupported method gate cannot silently exclude common methods.

acceptance_criteria.text: With `GET /x` registered, tokens `FOO`, `get` and `Get` on `/x` yield unsupported method. [D-066; loop W residual]
Token `PROPFIND` on a path no pattern matches yields unsupported method, not no match. [wave decision: lookup result order]

candidate_matches.title: Router lookup returns six result kinds and builds no response
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall make Router lookup return exactly the six RouteMatch kinds and never build HTTP responses, so that the wave 3 dispatcher maps kinds to 404/405/204/426/501 and adapters rely on that split.
candidate_matches.reason: Exactly six RouteMatch outcome kinds and dispatcher405/204 mapping conflict with ordered layer cursors and common404/OPTIONS200; preserve engine-free response ownership.

acceptance_criteria.text: Router lookup returns one of exactly six RouteMatch kinds and the routing package builds no HTTP response.

candidate_matches.title: Internal RestApp implementation with deferred router build and freeze
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall provide in an internal package of `NaruServe-api` a `RestApp` implementation that holds the router and the dispatcher, parses each registered pattern at the registration call, records the registrations and the routing policy, builds the `Router` with that policy only at the route-table freeze, and rejects any registration or `routerPolicy` call after the freeze with `IllegalStateException`. Wave 3 adds no public factory for it.
candidate_matches.reason: Deferred frozen router build and NEW-only registration conflict with common after-listen registration.

acceptance_criteria.text: The implementation is a public class in a package documented as internal and not part of the API contract, it implements `RestApp`, and it holds the router and the dispatcher. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-393] Decision: the implementation is public class `DefaultRestApp` in package `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal`, whose package javadoc states it is not API. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-14]
A registration with an invalid pattern (one that `RoutePattern.parse` rejects) throws at the registration call itself, before any freeze. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-047; D-048]

`app.get("/a/b", h)` followed by `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy.builder().mergeSlashes(true).build())` makes `GET /a//b` reach `h` after the harness freeze, showing the policy applies to registrations made before it. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; FR-ROUTE-006]

The `Router` is constructed only at the freeze, and a duplicate of D-044 surfaces as the freeze's `RoutingConfigException`, not at the second registration call. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-044] Decision: the freeze propagates the `RoutingConfigException` unchanged and leaves the app unfrozen, so `dispatcher()` keeps throwing `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-12]

After the harness freeze, `app.get(...)`, `app.route(Method, path, h)`, `app.route(MethodSet, path, h)` and `app.routerPolicy(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException`, and `RouteBuilder` registration methods (`get`, `put`, ...) throw `IllegalStateException` too, including on a builder obtained from `app.route(path)` before the freeze. [wave decision: Settings after the freeze] Decision: the internal WebSocket-route hook also throws `IllegalStateException` after the freeze, and a refused call records nothing. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-13]
No public static method or constructor in package `com.snoworca.naruserve` returns a `RestApp` in wave 3. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-111]

The internal implementation (not the public `RestApp` interface) offers an internal WebSocket-route registration hook that records a WebSocket registration and passes it to `Router.addWebSocket` at the freeze; the test-fixtures harness uses it to register a WebSocket-only route, and wave 3 dispatches no handshake to that route (a matching upgrade request gets the same `426` as a plain `GET`) until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; wave decision: Working app in wave 3]

candidate_matches.title: Request path, raw path and path parameter accessors
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall make `req.path()` return the decoded path without the query string, `req.rawPath()` return the raw, undecoded path without the query string, and `req.param(name)` return the decoded value of a variable of the matched pattern and throw an exception for a name absent from that pattern.
candidate_matches.reason: Scalar non-null params/full decoded path conflict with list/optional captures and mounted path views.

acceptance_criteria.text: For `GET /files/a%20b?x=1` matched by `/files/:name`, `req.path()` returns `/files/a b`. [D-073] Decision: `req.path()` percent-decodes the raw path once as UTF-8, keeps `+` as `+`, and applies no `mergeSlashes`, trailing-slash or case policy. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-1] Under `mergeSlashes(true)`, `GET /a//b` matched by `/a/b` gives `req.path()` = `/a//b` (the policy affects only route matching, not the decoded path). [wave 3 implementation decision]
For the same request `req.rawPath()` returns `/files/a%20b`, without `?x=1`. [D-074; wave decision: Remaining markers]
For the same request `req.param("name")` returns `a b`. [D-075]

`req.param("missing")` for a name not in the matched pattern throws an exception instead of returning `null`. [D-075] Decision: the exception is `IllegalArgumentException` and its message contains the name. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-2]

candidate_matches.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup (wave 4)
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall provide a dispatcher that takes each exchange from an `HttpAdapter` that passed the lifecycle gate of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013, checks the asterisk-form `OPTIONS *` first, then rejects a raw path not starting with `/` with `400`, then rejects a raw path refused by the wave 2 path validator with `400`, and only then calls the router lookup and either runs the middleware pipeline and the matched `RouteHandler` with a `Request` and a `Response` or writes the automatic response, where the pre-request rejections are answered before any `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them, and the two `400` rejections carry the standard error body.
candidate_matches.reason: Preselect-one-route pipeline conflicts with mutable current layer/Route cursor.

acceptance_criteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. This order applies to requests that passed the lifecycle gate; the unrecognised-method-token `501` comes after the validator check and before a `Request` is built.

A raw path that the wave 2 `PathValidator` rejects is answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8`) without a router lookup, and the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding: `/%2e%2e` and `/a%2Fb` are answered `400`, while `/%252e%252e` reaches a `/:x` route with `req.param("x")` = `%2e%2e`. [wave-3 carried: path validator before lookup; D-052; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134] Decision: a pre-request `400` or `501` carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and the `Content-Length` of the standard body; for a `HEAD` method token the `Content-Length` is kept and no body bytes are written. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-14]

An unrecognised method token is answered `501`, a raw path not starting with `/` `400`, a validator rejection `400` and `OPTIONS *` `204`, each before a `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them; a recording global middleware, a recording `onError` and a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)` record that they were never called. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; D-422; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]
In every handler and middleware call `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; I-014]
The HTTP-level assertions of T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06 run as tests through the in-memory adapter and the harness in `./gradlew build`. [D-397]

candidate_matches.title: Asterisk-form OPTIONS and raw paths not starting with a slash (wave 4)
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall answer the asterisk-form request `OPTIONS *` (raw path `*`) with `204` and an `Allow` header listing the methods of `Method.any()`, without route lookup or path validation, and answer any other raw path that does not start with `/` with `400` and the standard error body.
candidate_matches.reason: Asterisk OPTIONS and pre-request checks require oracle-specific updated semantics.

acceptance_criteria.text: Through the in-memory adapter, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` with `Allow` listing exactly the methods of `Method.any()` in `Method` declaration order and no body, even when no route is registered. [D-442; loop D: V1-006/V2-004] Decision: the `OPTIONS *` answer has no `Content-Length` header. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-19]

`OPTIONS *` reaches neither the router lookup nor the path validator: with a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is still answered `204` with the `Allow` of AC-1 (not the validator's `400` for a raw path `*`), and `h` records no call. [D-442; D-052]

A raw path `abc` and a raw path `*` with method `GET` are each answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`) without route lookup, and the access log records one line for each. [D-442; wave-4 carried: standard error body; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]
The `OPTIONS *` and non-`/` cases are tested through the in-memory adapter in waves 3 and 4; their TinyHttpd counterparts are not asserted in this requirement. [I-021; wave decision: Adapter halves]

candidate_matches.similarity_basis: Direct named existing contract and code trace, not embedding estimate.
candidate_matches.title: Handler failure and unfinished-response handling through the wave 4 error path
candidate_matches.statement: The system shall answer an exception thrown by a handler or middleware through the error path of FR-APP-005, which gives the standard `500` error body while the response is not committed and no `onError` responded, abort the response when the exception is thrown after commit or while streaming, and, when the chain returns with the response not started and no `next.run()`, log a developer warning through the app logger and finish the response with the status and headers set so far and an empty body without waiting for a timeout.
candidate_matches.reason: Auto-ending an unfinished returned handler conflicts with pending/deferred common response lifetime.

acceptance_criteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `INTERNAL_ERROR`) through the harness when no `onError` is registered. [D-127; D-132; wave-4 carried: interim failure handling replaced]

A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` and header `X-A: 1` but before commit is answered `500` with the standard error body; the status and headers the handler set are dropped and the exception is not rethrown to the adapter. [D-127; D-132; D-134]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a handler can reach before wave 5) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; D-131; wave decision: abort() after completion]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()`, and a middleware that returns without responding or calling `next.run()`, each yield the status and headers set so far (`202` with `X-A: 1`, and `200` for the middleware case) with an empty body, the response is `COMPLETED`, and the app logger received one `warn` naming the method and path. [D-126] Decision: the finishing behaviour is a `warn` through the app logger followed by `end()`; with the response `STREAMING` the dispatcher runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread and logs no warning.

candidate_matches.statement: The system shall let each middleware invocation continue the chain at most once through `next.run()` or `next.error(e)`, return from `next.run()` only after every downstream middleware and the handler returned, deliver the response of a middleware that responds without calling `next.run()` with no later middleware or handler run, and throw `IllegalStateException` for a second continuation within one invocation and for a continuation after the response completed or the request ended.
candidate_matches.reason: Same-thread/single-use/initial-return continuation guards conflict with observed deferred/repeated/explicit post-response next.

acceptance_criteria.text: A middleware that calls `next.run()` twice gets `IllegalStateException` from the second call, and the downstream middleware and handler ran once. [D-122; T35]

[D-123] Decision: `next.run()` throws when the response is `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED` or the request has ended, and no downstream step runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-10]

A middleware that records a marker after `next.run()` returns sees the handler's marker already recorded and `res.isCommitted()` true for a handler that called `res.send(...)`. [D-124] Decision: an exception thrown downstream propagates out of `next.run()` unchanged and the dispatcher hands it to the error path once, so a middleware may wrap `next.run()` in `try`/`catch`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-11]
A middleware that writes `res.status(401).send("no")` and returns without `next.run()` delivers `401` with body `no`, and the later middleware and the handler record no call. [D-125; T36]

Calling `next.error(e)` after `next.run()` in the same invocation, or `next.run()` after `next.error(e)`, throws `IllegalStateException`; `next.error(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. [D-122; D-116] Decision: `next.run()` and `next.error(e)` together count as the single continuation of one invocation. Decision: `next.error(null)` throws before the continuation is consumed. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-12]
`next.run()` runs the downstream chain on the calling thread, and no middleware or handler runs after the dispatcher returned to the adapter for a non-streaming response. [D-128]

candidate_matches.statement: The system shall make a route lookup, which takes the raw method token, the request path and an upgrade flag, return an engine-free result that is exactly one of matched (handler, path parameters, actual method, route kind, automatic-`HEAD` flag), method mismatch (with an `Allow` set), automatic OPTIONS (with an `Allow` set), WebSocket-only, unsupported method or no match, chosen in this order: unsupported method; no match; matched; automatic OPTIONS; automatic `HEAD`; WebSocket-only; method mismatch.

acceptance_criteria.text: The result type exposes exactly six kinds and each lookup returns exactly one; the matched kind carries the handler, the path parameters, the actual method (the request method for a direct match, `GET` under automatic `HEAD` and for a WebSocket match; it does not decide the wave 3 `req.method()` value, D-398), the route kind and the automatic-`HEAD` flag, and the method-mismatch and automatic-OPTIONS kinds carry an `Allow` `MethodSet`. [D-390] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-1] A field a kind does not carry reads as null (handler, method, route kind, allow) and params reads as an empty map.

An unrecognised method token yields unsupported method even when no pattern matches the path, and a recognised method on a path no pattern matches yields no match. [wave decision: lookup result order]
On a matched path a route of the request method wins over automatic OPTIONS and automatic `HEAD`, which win over WebSocket-only, which wins over method mismatch. [wave decision: lookup result order]

The lookup takes the raw, undecoded path as received in the request target, so a lookup of `GET /files/%252e` against `GET /files/:name` yields `name` = `%2e`; the path is checked with the path validator before any result is chosen, so a rejected path such as `/a%zz` fails with `IllegalArgumentException` for every method token, and "whatever the path" elsewhere in this scope means whatever accepted path. The upgrade flag is ignored unless the method token is `GET`; registering a route after the freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, a lookup before a successful freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, and the routing configuration error is an exception type of its own (name decided under C-07), distinct from `IllegalStateException` and `IllegalArgumentException`.
